findings.claim: The design does not specify capability negotiation for the changed ordinary-send receipt semantics, so a modern client cannot establish that an older daemon will start an unavailable recipient’s ACK deadline at send time.
findings.location: Root spec: Message deadline contract; Invitation contract protocol negotiation; Risks and mitigations
findings.evidence: The message contract promises “For every new durable ACK-required ordinary send” an original deadline at “canonical committed send time plus that duration”, including “no binding” and “unavailable binding”. The explicit compatibility mechanism instead appears under invitations: “negotiate protocol capability/version before any mutation requiring the new representation”; subtree validation likewise requires negotiation for “new incompatible fields”. Ordinary ACK-required sends need not contain any new invitation field or new representation, yet their old availability-deferred semantics are precisely what this redesign changes. An old daemon can therefore accept a wire-compatible ordinary send while failing the new deadline contract unless a receipt-semantics capability/version gate or an explicit mixed-version limitation is specified. No such gate or mixed-version receipt test is named in the settled artifact.
